plugin_desc: Teltonika industrial cellular router SNMP collection (enterprise PEN 48690). Private increment: whole-device CPU utilization (cpuUsage, 0-100 percent, scalar GET with instance .0) as the headline device_cpu_usage, with HOST-RESOURCES hrProcessorLoad kept as a per-core fallback; UCD-SNMP memory (memTotalReal / memAvailReal, KB, used = total − free); and modem temperature (mTemperature, integer tenths of a degree Celsius, converted to °C at collection). Fan and power-supply health stay N/A on this fanless compact design. Interface traffic comes from the built-in IF-MIB table. Applicable brands/models — Teltonika RUT / TRB / RUTX industrial 4G/5G cellular routers (RutOS, PEN 48690).
name: Router

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: CPU utilization of the Teltonika cellular router as a 0-100 percentage. The private cpuUsage scalar is the preferred headline; HOST-RESOURCES hrProcessorLoad is kept as a per-core fallback when the enterprise scalar is absent. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload or abnormal traffic.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: Total physical memory of the Teltonika cellular router in bytes (UCD memTotalReal, KB×1024).

metrics.name: device_memory_free
metrics.description: Available physical memory of the Teltonika cellular router in bytes (UCD memAvailReal, KB×1024).

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: Used physical memory of the Teltonika cellular router in bytes (memTotalReal − memAvailReal, KB×1024).

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Memory utilization of the Teltonika cellular router, derived as 100×(total−free)/total.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Modem temperature of the Teltonika cellular router in degrees Celsius. mTemperature reports tenths of a degree and is divided by 10 at collection so stored values, dashboards and alerts are already in °C. High values can indicate enclosure heat buildup or modem thermal stress.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
